history.summary: IDENTITY UNVERIFIED: no web source was found for a 'Prithudakeshwar' or 'Pirthudakeshwar' temple at Pehowa (or anywhere). This file documents the closest verified referent - the Prithudak Tirtha, the sacred pool and ghat complex on the Saraswati at Pehowa (ancient Prithudaka). Prithudaka is named in the Mahabharata and Puranas; legend says King Prithu offered water to his ancestors on the bank of the Saraswati here, and tradition holds that Lord Rama performed his ancestors' last rites at the site. The Haryana State Gazetteer records Prajapati as having created the world and the four varnas at Prithudaka. The site is regarded as the 'Gaya of the North' for Pind Daan and Pitru rituals; Alexander Cunningham formally identified modern Pehowa with ancient Prithudaka in the 19th century. Pehowa Inscriptions of the Gurjara-Pratihara ruler Mihira Bhoja (9th c. CE) attest the town's importance as a horse market and administrative centre. Note: Pehowa town has several temples (including a well-known Shiva temple and the Kartikeya Temple, documented separately as seq 1557); the CSV name may refer to a small Shiva shrine at the tirtha, but no source confirms this.

name: Prithudak (Pirthudakeshwar) Temple
town_description: Pehowa is an ancient town in Kurukshetra district, Haryana, on the left bank of the (revived) Saraswati river, about 27 km west of Kurukshetra city. Known in antiquity as Prithudaka, it is one of Haryana's oldest pilgrimage centres, famed as the 'Gaya of the North' for Pind Daan and ancestral rites. 9th-century Gurjara-Pratihara inscriptions record it as a thriving horse market and administrative centre.
